boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along Moraga’s nearby corridors, each with one documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Moraga Commons Park: multi-use amenities
cards.subtitle: St. Mary’s Road corridor
cards.notes: Walk the perimeter and choose an amenity that suits the visit; the Town lists a bandshell, disc golf, picnic areas, playgrounds, skatepark, and splash feature.
cards.short_summary: A central park with several documented recreation options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town identifies Moraga Commons as a 40.2-acre multi-use park at 1425 St. Mary’s Road and lists its amenities.
cards.source_title: Moraga Commons Park | Town of Moraga
cards.access_notes: Town parks open one hour before sunrise and close one hour after sunset.

cards.title: Moraga Library: reading and meeting space
cards.subtitle: St. Mary’s Road corridor
cards.notes: Bring a book or use the library’s public facilities; confirm the day’s opening time before heading over, since the posted schedule varies by day.
cards.short_summary: A county-library stop with a meeting room and accessibility resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Contra Costa County Library lists Moraga Library at 1500 St. Mary’s Road and identifies a meeting room and assistive-technology features.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s posted hours before visiting.

cards.title: Moraga Center: pedestrian-oriented core
cards.subtitle: Moraga Road and Moraga Way corridor
cards.notes: Use the area as a walking-oriented connector between nearby destinations; the Town’s adopted plan describes commercial and recreational activity within this 187-acre area.
cards.short_summary: A named planning district around the town’s commercial core.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town describes the 187-acre Moraga Center Specific Plan area as providing opportunities for commercial and recreational activity.
cards.source_title: Moraga Center Specific Plan Implementation Project | Town of Moraga
cards.access_notes: This is a district rather than a single venue; follow normal pedestrian and roadway rules.

cards.title: Moraga Shopping Center: retail-core landmark
cards.subtitle: Moraga Road corridor
cards.notes: Use this named commercial-center landmark to orient a walk through Moraga Center, then choose any open business that fits your plans and budget.
cards.short_summary: A shopping center included in the Town’s Moraga Center planning area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town’s housing document describes Moraga Center around Moraga Road and Moraga Way and states that it includes the Moraga Shopping Center.
cards.source_title: Moraga 2023–2031 Housing Element | Town of Moraga
cards.access_notes: Individual businesses set their own hours and purchase requirements.

cards.title: West Commons Park: public-art meadow
cards.subtitle: Moraga Road corridor
cards.notes: Take the walking trail through the meadow and pause to view the public art; the Town describes the park as immediately west of Commons Park.
cards.short_summary: A small neighborhood park combining a meadow, art, trail, and picnic area.
cards.evidence_claim: Moraga’s General Plan identifies West Commons on the west side of Moraga Road and lists its public-art meadow, picnic area, and walking trail.
cards.source_title: Moraga General Plan 2040 | Town of Moraga
cards.access_notes: Use designated paths and observe posted park rules.

cards.title: Hacienda de las Flores: historic grounds
cards.subtitle: Donald Drive corridor
cards.notes: Walk the landscaped grounds and view the historic facilities from public areas; check the Town calendar first because parts of the site may be reserved.
cards.short_summary: A Town facility with historic buildings, lawn, and landscaped grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town describes Hacienda de las Flores as having four historic facilities, a great lawn, and landscaped grounds at 2100 Donald Drive.
cards.access_notes: Reserved facilities require advance arrangements; check availability with Town Parks and Recreation.

cards.title: Mulholland Ridge: ridge-trail views
cards.subtitle: Donald Drive corridor
cards.notes: Start from Donald Drive and stay on the ridge trails for a viewpoint-oriented walk; bring water and follow the Town’s posted trail and dog rules.
cards.short_summary: A 260-acre preserve with trails connecting toward Hacienda and Orinda.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town identifies Mulholland Ridge Open Space Preserve as a 260-acre park atop Donald Drive with ridge trails connecting to Hacienda de las Flores and Orinda trails.
cards.source_title: Mulholland Ridge Open Space Preserve | Town of Moraga
cards.access_notes: Dogs are off-leash only on the paved portion; they must be leashed on unpaved portions.

cards.title: Rancho Laguna Park: pollinator garden
cards.subtitle: Camino Pablo corridor
cards.notes: Look for the Monarch and Pollinator Habitat and read its interpretive signage; visiting during spring through fall aligns with the Town’s stated bloom period.
cards.short_summary: A park with a documented native and drought-tolerant pollinator garden.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town states that Rancho Laguna Park contains a 2,600-square-foot Monarch and Pollinator Habitat and Demonstration Garden with over 600 plants.
cards.source_title: Rancho Laguna Park | Town of Moraga
cards.access_notes: The Town lists the park at 2101 Camino Pablo and posts seasonal off-leash rules separately.

cards.title: Rheem Valley Shopping Center: everyday services
cards.subtitle: Moraga Road and Center Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the center as a practical errand stop and confirm individual storefront hours before going; the Town identifies retail, restaurant, and service uses on site.
cards.short_summary: A named commercial center with documented retail and service tenants.
cards.evidence_claim: A Town planning record describes Rheem Valley Shopping Center as a commercial center with retail, restaurant, and service uses, including its Center Street frontage.
cards.source_title: Rheem Valley Shopping Center Public Hearing Record | Town of Moraga
cards.access_notes: Individual businesses set their own hours and purchase requirements.

cards.title: Lafayette-Moraga Regional Trail: multi-use route
cards.subtitle: Moraga Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the Town’s trail map to choose a legal access point, then walk or ride at a pace suited to shared use and changing trail conditions.
cards.short_summary: A named regional-trail route shown on the Town’s Moraga trails map.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town’s trails page links to the Lafayette/Moraga Regional Trail, and its official trail map labels the Lafayette–Moraga Trail through Moraga.
cards.access_notes: The Town trail map states that trails open one hour before sunrise and close one hour after sunset.
